title: Steer a current plan
current: Steering writes a spec or definition of done the user gives into the strategy doc as given, under # Objective and # Done when, never narrows the scope or finish line without the user's OK, and asks for any cut as a decision request; the plan is done only when all of it is done. It takes operator-written goals and a high-level strategy plan and splits them into dashes that run in parallel and reach done soonest, each spec carrying only its own slice, a done test drawn from # Done when, its QA requirements and its dependency edges. It records ordering needs as dependency edges only for shared files or required results instead of hand-made waves, keeps chains flat and attaches each edge at the earliest stage that works, and vets each with a subagent for overengineering. It vets every item before staffing it, including items others filed, and puts vet fixes into the spec first. Prefer simplifying or deleting and avoid new DB fields or migrations. Present each vetted dash and every other decision one at a time with context and a recommendation; file only with explicit approval and keep the strategy doc current; dashes that only close the recorded # Done when are covered by the user's request, while new scope still needs approval. Explicit operator choices of Blitz, epic or task remain available. Major scope proposals explain what they add, why and the simplest alternative, including DB changes; reviewers check for these too. Anything Yoke should have done automatically but did not is a defect: before manual recovery, root-cause it with a subagent and file feedback; never report a workaround as routine. Standing decision, commit, verification-failure and discard rules live in the always-loaded AGENTS.md managed block. As work lands, judge it against the doc's # Done when, not closed items or the workers' own suites; name what is still missing and file, staff and evaluate it until every point is met, then seek decisions for the next set or propose and vet it when clear. After failed item delivery QA, confirm and staff correction ownership, arrange qualifying delivery, preserve the original owner, inspect notice delivery and arrange supported resume/restaff if the surface lacks automatic wake. A dependency notice reports facts; activation GO remains a steering instruction, manual by design rather than a missing automatic wake. PRINCIPAL-level launches, including restaff, require explicit operator approval because they consume far more tokens; ordinary staffing is unchanged. Every steering reply ends with Needs you: and each open operator ask on one line, or Nothing needs you.
